intent: Match existing v8 terrain painting; lower background contrast, not craft quality.

regions.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Image 1 is the BACKGROUND TILE to repaint. Image 2 is a rendered game preview: use ONLY the detailed playable GROUND along its bottom as the material-and-painting STYLE REFERENCE. The flat abstract background visible in image 2 is the rejected style; do not copy it. Repaint image 1 as a square reusable back-wall tile in the SAME visual family as the reference ground. The prior tile was oversimplified to smooth vector ribbons and looked cheap next to the ground. Correct that mismatch with hand-painted irregular broad material facets, layered matte material relief, soft broken contours, medium-scale variations and restrained painted surface detail. Do not simply brighten the old flat ribbons. Keep the craftsmanship and material identity of the floor while reducing background contrast, edge sharpness and smallest detail. Aim for approximately 60 percent of the floor's detail density, NOT two-tone cel-shading, NOT smooth plastic curves, NOT a photograph. Handcrafted 2D game painting, rounded broad forms, minimal fine linework. Use shallow diffuse lighting, no specular shine or deep photographic contrast. This is an evenly filled rear wall material sheet that can cover a huge world through repeated large tiles. No composed cavern vista, no central focal point or emblem, no tunnels or architectural openings, no vanishing point, floor, horizon, sky, characters, labels, borders or spotlights. Spread varied smaller and larger material masses asymmetrically over the full square. Continue patterns across opposite edges for repeat tiling, no vignette. Completely OPAQUE PNG; replace transparent gaps with subdued dark colored material, never transparency or pure black holes. Square requested 1536x1536. Entire tile stays dark and low contrast, most values in RGB 25–65, highlights below RGB 85. Darkened surface retains its material without becoming vector shapes. Preserve the regional hue family.
Paper cavern: warm weathered gray-brown, muted ash taupe. Thick compressed paper-earth strata with broad softened torn layers and shallow creased surfaces; mineral-paper wall rather than floating paper ribbons. Some layered folds bend across one another, with a few subdued graphite traces. Make organic edges irregular like the reference ground but quieter; no thin jagged shards, printed drawings, writing or sharp paper cuts.
